shadows.name: panel-shade
shadows.value: .panel-shade { position: relative; } .panel-shade::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 10px -10px -10px 10px; z-index: -1; background: url("/assets/shade.svg"); pointer-events: none; }
shadows.purpose: The Text-Mode Shade: one layer offset 10px down and right behind the panel, tiled with a 7x13 SVG of staggered rectangles in muted lavender (#b8b2c2) that reads as the ░ light-shade glyph and tiles seamlessly; the panel's fill hides the overlap. Identical in every band, behind the four main panels only (tako dev recording, routes panel, deploy run, platform editor); the panel firms its outer border to the strong hairline.

motion.name: mark-rise
motion.purpose: A mark rises from its 0.3em resting stroke (0.14em on pipeline commands, 0 on nav and footer links) to a full highlight on hover. The button instead mixes 18% paper text into coral over 0.15s and presses 1px over 0.1s. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: ease-rise
motion.purpose: The footer illustration's single 1100ms rise-in (opacity 620ms ease-out); disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Diagram reveals on the home page: benchmark bars grow from zero (0.9s), Takosophy stars, variable rings and glints scale in one by one (0.5s, 0.06s apart), then the Latin chart names fade in last (0.6s), each constellation 0.35s after the last, with no lines on entrance; hovering a principle draws its lines in once star to star (0.4s ease-out, var(--l) x 0.12s apart in figure order) at 90% and holds them while hovered, and leaving retracts them (0.3s ease-in); touch screens show the lines at rest, and reduced motion shows and hides them without transitions; staggered sub-second delays. Opacity-only stages use plain ease at 0.3s to 0.4s.

motion.name: reveal-once
motion.purpose: Each diagram plays its entrance once as it scrolls into view. The script sets the start state, so without JS or under reduced motion every diagram renders finished.

motion.name: deploy-playback
motion.purpose: The deploy run loops while its timeline is 40% in view: it plays through, holds the finished deploy for 3s, then restarts; leaving the screen stops it and returning restarts it from the beginning. No Replay or Play control. State changes fade over 0.3s; while playing, the serving wire flows (0.6s linear loop) and a health probe runs the new wire (0.9s ease-in loop). The static, no-JS and reduced-motion state is the finished deploy, still.

motion.name: request-trace-loop
motion.value: URL typed 2 chars per 16ms, TLS and route stages 320ms each, answer held 1.5s; idle step 0.9s then 1.4s
motion.purpose: The request trace loops GET /, logo.svg 304, /_tako/image, channels 101, storages PUT, idle and scaled to 0, then a cold start, only while 35% of the figure is on screen; leaving the screen ends the run. No Replay; under reduced motion or without JS it holds the first request, answered.

motion.name: spot-stretch
motion.value: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); hover scale(1.03, 1.06) from transform-origin 50% 67.8%
motion.purpose: The hero peek, the one animated spot, stretches up slightly on hover from its cut line at the window edge, so the cut never shows. The only other painted art is the still chill octopus in who-it's-for and the footer painting. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: spot-boop
motion.value: 0.6s ease-out keyframes: 25% scale(1.1, 0.86), 55% scale(0.95, 1.1), 100% scale(1); hearts 1.1s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), delays 0, 0.14s, 0.26s, rising 78px
motion.purpose: On click the hero peek squashes and springs back while three small coral SVG hearts pop in at its kissing mouth and drift up and apart; a repeat click restarts it. Off under reduced motion.

narrative.northStar: The Plain Technical Document, Full Bleed
narrative.overview:
The site is still a technical document on dark brand ink: real copy, commands, code, a terminal recording and outlined diagrams carry it, with no decorative layer on top; painted octopus art appears in exactly three places, the hero peek, the chill octopus in who-it's-for and the footer painting. The document runs edge to edge in full-bleed bands that alternate the deep ink ground and the raised brand ink, and every block takes its own form: a statement and its answer, a star chart of principles, a pipeline of commands set as display type, a routes panel, a deploy played back as a timeline, a live request trace, an editor, a spec list, a full-width bar chart, a ruled audience list. The one face is pushed to strong scale contrast, from 12px labels to the 96px hero headline. Diagrams may move to explain a sequence; apart from the hero spot, nothing else does. The page is marked up like an annotated document: links and actions sit on a low translucent highlighter stroke that rises to a full highlight on hover, and the four main panels cast a text-mode shadow in a light-shade pattern, as a terminal would draw one.

The rhythm is long and even: generous band padding, one subject per band, text measures held to roughly 44 to 62 characters, and the figures allowed to run large. Headlines are lowercase or sentence case and say a plain thing plainly. Each band carries one accent (coral, mint or gold), and that accent colors the band's whole heading and the marks inside it, so the bands read apart without changing their grounds.

Color stays reserved. Coral is the one solid action, the focus ring and the prompt, and owns exactly one full-bleed field: the closing band. Mint is Tako's result wherever a benchmark is charted, and with gold lives in data, diagrams and code, and as a band accent in headings and marks. The painted brand art, the hero peek, the chill octopus and the painted blog and footer illustrations are the only pictorial material, and they share the four brand colors. Japan appears as a quiet detail (the "built in Japan" footer note, the Tokyo server in the deploy run), never as a theme.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed bands alternating the deep ink ground (#1f1b2b) and brand ink (#2f2a44) under a static paper grain, so raised bands read as paper and ground bands as ink; a single coral closing field.
JetBrains Mono is the only typeface, everywhere, including social cards, at strong scale contrast with tight negative tracking on display sizes.
Each block has its own form, all drawn from the same hairlines, outlined boxes and type scale.
One solid coral button; every other control is marked text on a translucent stroke in its band's accent.
Every band heading but the closing one takes its band's accent as its whole color.
One shadow: a text-mode shade, a ░ light-shade tile in muted grey offset behind the four main panels. No blur, no outlines on buttons, no underlines on links.
Tako leads every benchmark in mint; competitors are grey.
Diagrams explain a sequence on scroll into view and render still without JS or under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Band Mark Rule
rules.body: Coral is the only solid action color: the one button, the focus ring, the Play button. Marks take their band's accent at 45% (coral outside the home bands), so a link in a mint band carries a mint stroke. Mint and gold never fill a button.

rules.name: The One Coral Field Rule
rules.body: Coral fills small things (the button, the Play button) and exactly one band: the closing call to action. No other band, panel or card is coral.

rules.name: The Tako Leads in Mint Rule
rules.body: Tako's result is mint wherever it is charted: the home bar chart, the performance line charts (at a heavier 3px stroke) and the performance social card. On bar charts every competitor is grey (muted lavender, then dim lavender). Line charts give competitors distinct hues only so each line can be followed (HAProxy coral, Envoy gold, Caddy muted lavender, nginx dashed dim lavender). Green reads as more; coral next to Tako's number would read as a warning.

rules.name: The Binding Palette Rule
rules.body: Coral, mint, gold and brand ink are fixed because the painted brand art, the blog and footer illustrations and the diagrams use them. Do not tune, tint or replace them.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Every role uses JetBrains Mono. Hierarchy comes from size and weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 700), with negative tracking only on 700-weight sizes of 22px and up. No second family, no italics outside code comments, no uppercase tracking.

rules.name: The Band Heading Rule
rules.body: Every band sets `data-accent` and its heading takes that accent as its whole color: hero coral, why mint, Takosophy gold, commands coral, dev mint, deploy coral, platform gold, defaults coral, benchmark mint, who-it's-for gold; the closing band stays deep ink on coral. Whole headings only: no colored words, no highlight spans, no gradient text, no label line above a heading. Headings stay lowercase or sentence case.

rules.name: The Stepped Scale Rule
rules.body: A heading takes the step its block earns: base section title by default, the larger step only for the why heading and diagram- or chart-led sections, display sizes only for the hero and the closing band.

rules.name: The Text-Mode Shade Rule
rules.body: Only the four main panels carry it: one layer offset 10px down and right, tiled with the ░ light-shade pattern in muted lavender, the same in every band, never blurred, never colored by the accent, never on hover or state. No other panel, card, button or text gets a shadow.

rules.name: The Spot Art Rule
rules.body: Painted octopus art appears on the page in exactly three places, each small and transparent: the hero peek over the recording window's edge, the chill octopus under the who-it's-for lead, and the footer painting. Never add a spot to another section, box painted art in a frame or card, run it full-bleed or give the hero a big painting column (tried and rejected as too heavy).

rules.name: The One Animated Spot Rule
rules.body: Only the hero peek moves; the chill octopus sits still, and the footer painting has only its single rise-in.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not lifted: borders at 14% off-white, strong borders at 32%, one tonal step of brand ink. Apart from the text-mode shade, no shadow, glow or blur is used for depth.

rules.name: The Paper Grain Rule
rules.body: Raised bands layer a static 220px SVG fractal-noise tile (warm off-white at about 9% alpha) over brand ink, the same grain the painted illustrations sit on, so raised bands read as paper and ground bands, which stay flat, as ink. The grain never moves, never tints per accent and is not used inside a band.

rules.name: The Run Ground Rule
rules.body: The deploy run, whose bars need a ground that is not the band's, takes brand ink on the ground and drops to the deep ground on a raised band. Other panels keep the deep ground and, where they share the band's tone, are held apart by the strong hairline and the shade.

rules.name: The Explaining Motion Rule
rules.body: Diagrams may animate to explain a sequence: once on scroll into view, or, for the deploy run and the request trace, in a loop that runs only while it is on screen. Every diagram renders finished or still without JS or under reduced motion. Decorative motion on non-diagram content is still out, with one exception: the hero spot's hover stretch and click squash (The One Animated Spot Rule), which reduced motion stills.

dos: Do set every text role in JetBrains Mono and build hierarchy from size and weight.
Do build pages from full-bleed bands that alternate the ground and brand ink, and give each block its own form.
Do put two-column blocks on the one shared split (1fr 1fr, clamp(40px, 5vw, 96px) gap, top-aligned).
Do use coral (#e88783) for the one solid button, the focus ring and the prompt, and keep it to one full-bleed field.
Do keep mint and gold inside data, status, diagrams, code and band accents, and chart Tako in mint with competitors in grey.
Do give every band a `data-accent` and color its whole heading and its marks with it; the closing band keeps ink on coral.
Do mark links and secondary actions with the 0.3em translucent stroke that rises to a full highlight on hover; quiet controls take the neutral ink mark.
Do put the text-mode shade, in muted lavender, behind the four main panels and nothing else, and clear it with a 28px caption gap.
Do keep the one 3px radius and the single tonal step between ground and brand ink.
Do let a diagram animate to explain a sequence, and render it finished or still without JS or under reduced motion.
Do keep painted octopus art to the hero peek, the chill octopus and the footer painting, and animate only the peek.
Do lay the static paper grain over raised bands so they read as paper against flat ink ground bands.
Do keep Japan to small, quiet details.
donts: Don't use soft shadows, glows, gradients or blur, or the shade outside the four main panels.
Don't outline buttons, or underline links (dotted or solid); controls are marked, not bordered.
Don't use pill buttons, large rounded cards, or a light ground.
Don't color single words or highlight phrases inside headlines, or put a small label line above a heading.
Don't chart Tako's result in coral.
Don't animate band backgrounds (drifting glyph fields, flow-line currents, request lanes) or tint band grounds per accent; tried and rejected because every band looked the same.
Don't add a second typeface, or uppercase tracked labels.

Don't add decorative motion to non-diagram content; outside diagrams, the footer illustration's single rise-in is the only entrance animation and the hero spot's hover and click the only interactive motion, and both respect reduced motion.

Don't add a mascot or spot to any other section, copy the clothing or design of the "Chill Guy" meme character in the chill octopus, box painted art, run it full-bleed or at column size, or give the hero a big painting column.
Don't alter the four binding brand colors.
